label: neiso 57 dynamic rr
definition: (PROBE — winter scarcity charter Limb A; keeper promotion is the owner's call.) The 2026-07-09-neiso-56-reserve-coopt keeper recipe + neiso_dynamic_reserve_requirements: the in-LP co-opt families' static published 1,800/1,200/600 MW requirements replaced by the MEASURED as-enforced hourly reserve-requirement series (ISO-NE ISO Express 'Hourly Reserve Requirements', system ROS row; mean ~2,300 MW, above static in all 26,280 train hours; the NYISO #1344 analogue, rule-13 measured market-design input, zero fitted parameters). RESULT: the co-opt ENGAGES for the first time on NEISO — the 2025-06-24 18:00 heat-wave hour binds the measured 2,909 MW requirement on the scored P2 pass, stacking a $125 RCPF (system max $397, the model's first >$300 train-year hour, landing ON an actual DA>$300 hour). C3c 2025 improves 0h -> 1h vs DA 12h (still short of the [6,24]h gate); C5b unchanged (0.827 vs 2.08 TWh). SEASONAL CORRECTION: the actual DA tail is winter only in 2023; 2024 and 11/12 of 2025 hours are summer heat-wave evening peaks. C3a/C3b/C1 no regression.
market_story: With the measured requirement the reserve constraint finally has the MW ISO-NE actually enforces: in the June 2025 heat wave the fleet's spare headroom drops below the enforced 2,909 MW 30-min requirement for one evening hour, so the RCPF prices into the LMP exactly as ISO-NE's real-time co-optimization does — the model's first structurally-formed scarcity hour, landing on an actual DA>$300 hour. The zero-forcing twin binds the same event deeper (2h, dual to $250): the winter-fuel/reliability floors keep low-output units on line whose remaining headroom carries reserve, mirroring the reliability commitments the real market makes; stripping them makes the system reserve-shorter, not looser.
